key_insight: Oxide-cap position alters aluminum-particle combustion: front caps enhance local evaporation near the cap–metal junction, while rear caps absorb heat and lower reaction temperatures.
engineering_relevance: Cap-aware evaporation and drag models can improve Lagrangian predictions of burning aluminum particles without resolving each particle’s boundary layer.
method: Boundary-layer resolved simulations varying cap size, cap orientation, and particle Reynolds number.
Revised spherical-particle modeling using a 0.55-rule for film-state properties and optimized evaporation and drag correlations.
Extended modeling to capped doublet particles using exposed aluminum area and a front-cap evaporation correction.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports good agreement between optimized correlations and simulations, with integrated heat release generally tracking evaporation rate, but provides no numerical error metrics.
watch_item: Exposed-area scaling alone is insufficient for front caps, particularly at high particle Reynolds numbers, where evaporation-flux corrections are needed.
paper_title: Influence of an oxide cap on the combustion of aluminum particles using boundary-layer resolved simulations
